title: AI productivity gains are closer to 10% than 10x
excerpt: The benchmark is wrong, not the results.
content_html:
You have 1 article left to read this month before you need to register a free LeadDev.com account.

Key takeaways:

  • AI adoption is up 65%, but median PR throughput rose just 8%.
  • Coding is only ~16% of engineer time, so speeding it up barely moves overall throughput.
  • To close the gap, target AI at non-coding bottlenecks, and track utilization, impact, and cost together.

Most engineering leaders I talk to are quietly worried they’re falling behind.

AI models and coding tools are launching constantly, often with claims of 3x or 10x productivity improvements. When their teams see more modest results, they assume something is wrong.

The concern is understandable. But in most cases, it’s the benchmark that’s wrong,  not the results.

Our team at DX analyzed engineering velocity from November 2024 to February 2026 across a sample from 400+ companies where AI adoption rose sharply. We found a 7.76% median increase in PR throughput – the best, though imperfect, proxy metric we currently have for directionally measuring velocity. 

That’s a real gain. It’s also well below what most leaders expect, and well below what vendor marketing typically promises.

If your numbers are in that range, you are not behind. You are in line with the industry.

What the data actually shows

Our sample covered technology, financial services, retail, and healthcare companies ranging from approximately 150 to 10,000 engineers. During the study period, AI tool usage increased by an average of 65%. Median PR throughput increased by 7.76%.

The mean gain was 13.1%, higher than the median due to a small number of high-performing companies. Even at the 90th percentile, gains approached 44% — still far below the order-of-magnitude improvements often cited in executive circles.

For most organizations, today’s AI coding tools are delivering a 5–15% throughput gain. To put that in concrete terms: an organization with 500 engineers seeing a 10% improvement means potentially shipping 10% more value per engineer,  without the headcount cost. That is a meaningful return. The mistake is measuring it against an expectation of 2–3x productivity gains.

Why the gap exists

If AI adoption increased 65%, why has throughput moved less than 8% at the median? We interviewed developers across our sample to understand what’s holding them back.

Coding isn’t the main bottleneck. 

AI accelerates code generation, but coding represents approximately 16% of how engineers spend their time. Even cutting that time in half doesn’t meaningfully move overall throughput. As one developer put it: “A four-day task might take three. But that doesn’t mean I’m shipping 3x more PRs.”

New bottlenecks emerge

AI has accelerated code generation, but code review and integration remain largely unassisted. Several developers described time saved writing code being consumed by the extra scrutiny AI-generated output requires, resulting in a net-zero productivity gain.

Skill and tooling gaps compound each other. 

Effective use of  AI tools and agents is its own discipline, and most developers are still early in developing it. Immature tools steepen the learning curve; developers early on the curve extract less value. 

In our research, we have found that every business firmographic and developer demographic undergoes a measurable J-curve in speed and quality when first learning about these tools. With additional practice and education, this curve corrects, and advanced users consistently outperform their peers.

AI tools lack institutional context. 

AI performs well on self-contained, well-documented problems. Most real engineering work is neither. The context typically lives in people’s heads or is distributed across heterogeneous systems of record.

Three steps to unlock more from AI investment

The 5–15% gains we’re seeing today are not the ceiling. Closing the gap between current results and the potential of AI will require looking beyond code generation. 

Based on our research, here’s where I’d focus.

  • AI tools are amplifiers. They take what developers are already doing and scale it, for better or worse. A well-documented, well-structured codebase with low friction makes it easier for developers to use AI effectively. Poor documentation and high friction make it harder. Assess your codebases and workflows at the service and team level before scaling AI use.
  • Since coding represents only ~14% of a developer’s time, the highest-leverage opportunities are likely elsewhere: in planning, code review, documentation, and operations. Use developer experience surveys and system telemetry to identify where friction is highest, then direct AI investment toward those specific pain points.
  • Increased velocity from AI comes with risks that, left unmonitored, can erode the gains. Track not just whether throughput is improving, but whether that improvement is coming at a cost. The DX AI Measurement Framework covers three dimensions – utilization, impact, and cost – giving leaders validated signals across the full AI adoption lifecycle. This multi-dimensional approach matters, because improvements in one dimension can come at the expense of another.

Where to focus next

The organizations that capture the next wave of AI-driven productivity gains will be the ones that invest in the full breadth of their development lifecycle and in the human and contextual conditions that allow AI to be effective.

That starts with three steps: assess your foundational readiness by service and team; identify where the highest-leverage AI opportunities exist; and measure progress using validated signals across utilization, impact, and cost.

The gains are real. The ceiling is higher than where most organizations are today. Getting there requires a more complete view of where AI coding tools are and aren’t working.

content_html_zh:
本月您还剩 1 篇文章需要阅读，然后您需要注册免费的 LeadDev.com 帐户。

要点：

  • 人工智能的采用率上升了 65%，但公关吞吐量中位数仅上升了 8%。
  • 编码仅占工程师时间的 16%，因此加快编码速度几乎不会提高整体吞吐量。
  • 为了缩小差距，将人工智能瞄准非编码瓶颈，并一起跟踪利用率、影响和成本。

我采访过的大多数工程领导者都暗自担心自己落后了。

人工智能模型和编码工具不断推出，通常声称生产力提高了 3 倍或 10 倍。 当他们的团队看到较为温和的结果时，他们就会认为出了问题。

这种担忧是可以理解的。 但在大多数情况下，错误的是基准，而不是结果。

我们的 DX 团队对 2024 年 11 月至 2026 年 2 月期间人工智能采用率急剧上升的 400 多家公司的样本进行了分析。 我们发现 PR 吞吐量中值增加了 7.76%——这是我们目前用于定向测量速度的最佳代理指标，尽管并不完美。

这才是真正的收获。 它也远低于大多数领导者的预期，也远低于供应商营销通常的承诺。

如果你的数字在这个范围内，那么你就没有落后。 你符合这个行业。

数据实际显示了什么

我们的样本涵盖技术、金融服务、零售和医疗保健公司，工程师数量从大约 150 到 10,000 名不等。 研究期间，AI 工具的使用率平均增加了 65%。 PR 吞吐量中位数增长了 7.76%。

由于业绩良好的公司数量较少，平均涨幅为 13.1%，高于中位数。 即使在第 90 个百分位数，收益也接近 44%，仍然远低于高管圈子经常引用的改进幅度。

对于大多数组织而言，当今的 AI 编码工具可实现 5-15% 的吞吐量增益。 具体来说：一个拥有 500 名工程师的组织看到 10% 的改进意味着每个工程师的价值可能增加 10%，而无需增加人员成本。 这才是有意义的回报。 错误在于根据生产率提高 2-3 倍的预期来衡量。

为什么存在差距

如果人工智能的采用率增加了 65%，为什么吞吐量的中位数变化不到 8%？ 我们采访了样本中的开发人员，以了解是什么阻碍了他们。

编码不是主要瓶颈。

人工智能可加速代码生成，但编码约占工程师花费时间的 16%。 即使将时间减少一半也不会显着提高整体吞吐量。 正如一位开发人员所说：“四天的任务可能需要三天。 但这并不意味着我的 PR 数量增加了 3 倍。”

新的瓶颈出现

人工智能加速了代码生成，但代码审查和集成在很大程度上仍然没有得到帮助。 几位开发人员表示，编写代码所节省的时间被人工智能生成的输出所需的额外审查所消耗，从而导致净零生产力增益。

技能和工具差距相互加剧。

有效使用人工智能工具和代理是它自己的学科，大多数开发人员仍处于开发早期。 不成熟的工具使学习曲线变得陡峭；处于曲线早期的开发人员提取的价值较少。

在我们的研究中，我们发现，当第一次了解这些工具时，每个企业和开发人员群体在速度和质量方面都会经历可测量的 J 曲线。 通过额外的实践和教育，这条曲线会得到纠正，高级用户的表现将始终优于同龄人。

人工智能工具缺乏制度背景。

人工智能在独立、有据可查的问题上表现良好。 大多数实际工程工作都不是。 上下文通常存在于人们的头脑中或分布在异构记录系统中。

从人工智能投资中释放更多潜力的三个步骤

我们今天看到的 5-15% 的涨幅还不是上限。 缩小当前结果与人工智能潜力之间的差距需要超越代码生成。

根据我们的研究，这就是我要关注的地方。

  • 人工智能工具是放大器。 他们采用开发人员已经在做的事情并对其进行扩展，无论好坏。 文档齐全、结构良好且摩擦力低的代码库使开发人员更容易有效地使用人工智能。 糟糕的文档和高摩擦使得事情变得更加困难。 在扩展 AI 使用之前，在服务和团队级别评估您的代码库和工作流程。
  • 由于编码只占开发人员大约 14% 的时间，因此影响力最高的机会可能在其他地方：规划、代码审查、文档和运营。 使用开发人员体验调查和系统遥测来确定摩擦最大的地方，然后将人工智能投资导向这些特定的痛点。
  • 人工智能提高速度会带来风险，如果不加以监控，可能会侵蚀收益。 不仅要跟踪吞吐量是否有所提高，还要跟踪这种改进是否会付出代价。 DX AI 测量框架涵盖三个维度：利用率、影响和成本，为领导者在整个 AI 采用生命周期中提供经过验证的信号。 这种多维度的方法很重要，因为一个维度的改进可能会以牺牲另一个维度为代价。

接下来要关注哪里

那些能够抓住下一波人工智能驱动的生产力提升浪潮的组织将是那些在其开发生命周期的全部范围以及使人工智能发挥作用的人力和环境条件上进行投资的组织。

首先分为三个步骤：通过服务和团队评估您的基础准备情况；确定哪里存在最具杠杆作用的人工智能机会；并使用经过验证的信号来衡量利用率、影响和成本方面的进展。

收获是真实的。 上限比当今大多数组织的上限要高。 要实现这一目标，需要更全面地了解人工智能编码工具在哪里工作、在哪里不工作。
